argument: For dx=2,dy=6, column sampling uses 3 pixels while row sampling uses 7, with each successive row represented; the latter removes the stated gaps.
The octant explicitly uses upward y; NE therefore increments both x and y. The alternatives move north only or southeast.
An ascending integer range starting above its endpoint is empty under the usual loop convention. Swapping endpoints preserves the geometric segment and supplies valid ascending bounds.
The set {(4,j):j=1,...,5} includes both endpoints and every intervening row. A slope quotient is undefined and one pixel cannot represent the five-row segment.
At D=0 the ideal line passes exactly through the midpoint, so E and NE are equally close. Either tie rule can be designed, but the given ≥ rule deterministically chooses NE.
The candidate set permits at most one upward unit per rightward unit, so after two x steps it can rise at most two, not five. An axis swap is mathematically necessary for this formulation.
At the next x=3, ideal height is 6/5=1.2, below midpoint 1.5, so E=(3,1) is closer than NE=(3,2). This separately checks the decision sign.
Mapping upward y to screen v=v0-y sends a +1 y step to a -1 v step. Copying NE=(x+1,y+1) literally into downward screen coordinates reverses its visual vertical direction.
Writing F(x,y)=2*dy*(x+1)-2*dx*y-dx, direct subtraction F(x+1,y+1)-F(x,y)=2*dy-2*dx proves the update for all allowed integer dx,dy.
